question: In the United States, for Q4 2019 and Q4 2020, first select only those cities where total sales (with no promotions) rose by at least 20% from Q4 2019 to Q4 2020. Among these cities, rank products by their overall sales (still excluding promotions) in those quarters and take the top 20%. Then compute each top product’s share of total sales in Q4 2019 and Q4 2020 and calculate the difference in share from Q4 2019 to Q4 2020, returning the results in descending order of that share change.
sql:
WITH city_sales AS (
    SELECT c.cust_city, t.calendar_year, t.calendar_quarter_number, SUM(s.amount_sold) as total_sales 
    FROM sales s 
    JOIN customers c ON s.cust_id = c.cust_id 
    JOIN times t ON s.time_id = t.time_id 
    WHERE c.country_id = 52790 AND t.calendar_quarter_number = 4 AND t.calendar_year IN (2019, 2020) AND s.promo_id = 999 
    GROUP BY c.cust_city, t.calendar_year, t.calendar_quarter_number
),
city_growth AS (
    SELECT 
        cust_city,
        SUM(CASE WHEN calendar_year = 2019 THEN total_sales ELSE 0 END) as q4_2019_sales,
        SUM(CASE WHEN calendar_year = 2020 THEN total_sales ELSE 0 END) as q4_2020_sales
    FROM city_sales
    GROUP BY cust_city
    HAVING SUM(CASE WHEN calendar_year = 2020 THEN total_sales ELSE 0 END) >= 1.2 * SUM(CASE WHEN calendar_year = 2019 THEN total_sales ELSE 0 END)
),
qualifying_cities AS (
    SELECT cust_city FROM city_growth
),
product_sales AS (
    SELECT 
        c.cust_city,
        s.prod_id,
        t.calendar_year,
        t.calendar_quarter_number,
        SUM(s.amount_sold) as product_sales
    FROM sales s
    JOIN customers c ON s.cust_id = c.cust_id
    JOIN times t ON s.time_id = t.time_id
    WHERE c.country_id = 52790 
        AND c.cust_city IN (SELECT cust_city FROM qualifying_cities)
        AND t.calendar_quarter_number = 4 
        AND t.calendar_year IN (2019, 2020)
        AND s.promo_id = 999
    GROUP BY c.cust_city, s.prod_id, t.calendar_year, t.calendar_quarter_number
),
product_overall_sales AS (
    SELECT 
        prod_id,
        SUM(product_sales) as overall_sales
    FROM product_sales
    GROUP BY prod_id
),
product_ranked AS (
    SELECT 
        prod_id,
        NTILE(100) OVER (ORDER BY overall_sales DESC) as sales_rank,
        overall_sales
    FROM product_overall_sales
)
SELECT COUNT(*), COUNT(DISTINCT prod_id) as distinct_products, COUNT(DISTINCT sales_rank) as distinct_ranks
FROM product_ranked
